newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SingTel new service targets small firms.
newsitem.headline: SingTel new service targets small firms.

text.p: Singapore Telecommunications Ltd (SingTel) launched on Thursday an electronic trading service targetted at small to medium-sized firms.
SingTel officials said it would providing a cheaper alternative than other systems for buying or selling products and services through the Internet.

"By deploying electronic commerce services at cost effective rates, SingTel aims to help major corporations as well as the small to medium-sized enterprises to increase their competitive edge in the global market," Lee Hsien Yang, president and chief executive officer of SingTel said.

Lee said the new service, STEMS INTER*change, jointly developed by SingTel and U.S. systems integration firm Control Data Systems, was developed especially for the small to medium-sized firms accounting for 80 percent of retail trade.
Most had thus far shied away from electronic trading due to high start-up costs.
STEMS INTER*change service is cheaper than the conventional Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) setup, where information is also exchanged using computers.
No sophisticated software is needed by users of STEM INTER*change service, who only require a Web browser and an Internet dial-up account.

Company officials expect the new service, which had a start-up cost of Singapore $2 million, to bring in a similar amount within a year of the launch but said the estimate was "on the conservative side" given the potential of the market.

"It's an emerging market. The project is very young. It will not be a core business for SingTel but it will be a major player among our new services in Electronic commerce," Leong Shin Loong, SingTel's assistant vice president of multimedia
Singapore Airlines is the first customer, using the service to procure goods and services electronically from suppliers in Singapore and overseas, they said.
